title: Exceptional point structure and chiral state transfer in a rate-operator-engineered $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric Bose-Hubbard dimer
authors: Jaakko Luomala, Federico Settimo, Kimmo Luoma, Iiro Vilja, Jyrki Piilo
abstract: The rate operator quantum jumps (ROQJ) is a general method to unravel a master equation describing the dynamics of an open quantum system into stochastic pure state trajectories. By post-selecting on no jumps occurring, one obtains a trajectory generated by a non-Hermitian Hamiltonian. The ROQJ allows for versatile modification of this non-Hermitian evolution, with each non-Hermitian Hamiltonian corresponding to a different continuous measurement scheme. We apply the ROQJ to modify the non-Hermitian dynamics of the open three-particle Bose-Hubbard dimer model under environmental non-local dephasing to construct a $PT$-symmetric non-Hermitian Hamiltonians with a general two parameter $PT$-symmetric imaginary diagonal part, which generalizes the well-known gain-loss Bose-Hubbard dimer. We characterize the symmetry structure of the spectrum for different on-site interaction strengths. For vanishing on-site interaction, we find the unbroken $PT$-symmetry region enclosed by order two exceptional lines of different character and four order four exceptional points, two of which are not found in the usual gain-loss Bose-Hubbard dimer. Additionally, we find regions with degenerate imaginary parts of the eigenvalues, also not found in the gain-loss Bose-Hubbard dimer. In this parameter space, we use time-dependent rate operator transformations to investigate state transfer under slowly varying parameter loops. Loops encircling an order four exceptional point exhibit chiral state transfer. Because the loops cross exceptional lines, the final states are superpositions of eigenstates. Chiral state transfer is also found with non-zero homogeneous on-site interaction when the loop crosses over broken $PT$-symmetry regions of different character. Using inhomogeneous on-site interactions, we find direction dependent state transfer between eigenstates without crossing or encircling exceptional points.
summary: This paper applies the Rate Operator Quantum Jumps formalism to analyze an open Bose-Hubbard dimer model, constructing a $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric non-Hermitian Hamiltonian. The study maps out the parameter space containing exceptional points and demonstrates that traversing closed loops around these points induces chiral state transfer. This offers a powerful method for controlling quantum dynamics in open systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the exceptional point structure and chiral state transfer in an open Bose-Hubbard dimer model engineered using rate-operator quantum jumps.
main_result: The research demonstrates that encircling specific exceptional points leads to chiral state transfer, and direction-dependent state transfer can be achieved even without crossing EPs using inhomogeneous interactions.
method: The authors employ the Rate Operator Quantum Jumps (ROQJ) formalism to derive a $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric non-Hermitian Hamiltonian from the system's master equation, followed by time-dependent analysis of parameter loops.
model_or_system: The system is an open three-particle Bose-Hubbard dimer model subjected to environmental non-local dephasing. The dynamics are governed by a master equation, which is then mapped onto an effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian via ROQJ.
key_observables: Exceptional Points (EPs), $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetry breaking/restoring regions, chiral state transfer, and direction-dependent state transfer.
important_parameters: On-site interaction strength ($U$), and transformation parameters ($k, l$).
main_assumptions: The dynamics are modeled using the Markovian GKSL master equation, and the analysis relies on the pure state trajectories derived from ROQJ.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams showing the boundaries between unbroken and broken $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetry regions in the parameter space, and plots show the evolution of eigenvalues and state amplitudes as parameters are varied.
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the ROQJ method to construct the $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric non-Hermitian Hamiltonian. It then characterizes the symmetry structure by mapping out the parameter space containing EPs. Finally, it uses time-dependent rate operator transformations to simulate state transfer dynamics around these critical points.
why_interesting: This work provides a sophisticated theoretical framework for controlling open quantum systems by engineering non-Hermitian Hamiltonians, linking concepts like $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetry breaking, exceptional points, and non-adiabatic dynamics to physical observables like state transfer.
